name: Rust Spewer
body:
Rust Spewer
CR 3

This heavyset creature hops awkwardly on four legs, its skin warty and toadlike. Droplets fall off its trumpet-like mouth, and you see them hiss and burn through the ground.

XP 800
N Medium magical beast
Init +2; Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision; Perception +7

DEFENSE

AC 15, touch 13, flat-footed 12 (+2 Dex, +1 dodge, +2 natural)
hp 34 (4d10+12)
Fort +7, Ref +6, Will +2
Immune acid

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft.
Melee tongue +6 (1d8 acid plus rust), 2 claws +6 (1d4+2)
Ranged spittle +7 touch (1d8 acid plus rust)

STATISTICS

Str 15, Dex 14, Con 17, Int 2, Wis 12, Cha 6
Base Atk +4; CMB +6; CMD 19 (23 vs. trip)
Feats Dodge, Weapon Focus (spittle)
Skills Perception +7, Stealth +6

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Rust (Ex)

Acid of rust spewers has highly oxidizing properties, causing any metal object it touches to swiftly rust and corrode. The object touched takes half its maximum hp in damage and gains the broken condition—a second hit destroys the item. An attended object or any magic object can attempt a DC 15 Fortitude save to negate this effect. If hit by a rust spewer’s tongue or spittle, any metal armor that the creature hit wears is subject to this effect. Against creatures made of metal, a rust spewer deals double acid damage. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Spittle (Ex)

A rust spewer’s spittle has a maximum range of 30 ft., with no range increment.

ECOLOGY

Environment any
Organization solitary, pair, or pack (3–14)
Treasure none

Rust spewers are highly territorial, four-legged creatures that have a strong tendency to live in packs, rarely being encountered in groups smaller than three. In that they resemble wolves, although this is where the resemblance ends. A rust spewer resembles a hideous combination between a toad and an insect. It is four legged and can walk, but moves mainly by hopping short distances, for reasons unknown. When it sees a potential victim, which includes about anything that moves, it stands on its hind legs and hurls globs of thick, adhesive and highly acidic saliva until the enemy stops moving. Rust spewers don’t have teeth or jaws and thus digest their prey externally, their acid melting their future meal until it becomes a liquid sludge that they then slurp up with their trumpet-like, extended mouths.

Due to their low mobility, packs of rust spewers often lair in a single stretch of territory, migrating only when lack of prey forces them to. They don’t fear humanoids, though rarely risk approaching civilization. Small groups of adventurers are one of their favorite meals, as they disturbingly enjoy slurping a warrior out of his thoroughly rusted armor that barely holds in the slush that was previously its owner.

While they do indeed flee when faced with overwhelming odds, rust spewers do not have a great sense of self preservation, accustomed to overcoming adversity with their range superiority. Even larger and more ferocious creatures, like bears and boars, are quickly reduced to soup, sometimes not even able to charge and tear apart even a single one of those creatures before their painful demise. In the wilds that aren’t home to some stronger monsters, rust spewers are rarely in danger and seldom die from violence. Their survivability is further increased by the fact that the creature’s meat is borderline inedible. Even ignoring the fact that cutting into them makes contact with their extremely potent acid almost a certainty, their tough flesh has a disgusting taste which only a starving creature would tolerate.

Rust spewers breed slowly and only when food is abundant. They live their lives at a slow pace when not hunting or defending themselves and do not like to wander too much. They can live in almost any non-extreme environment, though are mostly encountered in warm and temperate climates, like rocky or grassy plains, especially those that get just enough sun for their hide to blend in with the background. An average rust spewer is 4 feet tall and weighs 170 pounds. Its warty skin resembles a dried-out pickle in texture and color.

This massive elk is covered in white, matted fur. Its majestic, thick antlers span 15 feet but the head they grace is terrifying. Blue, glowing eyes above a smiling grimace of sharp teeth.
